sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们能做什么？

sentences.en: and another department store tells us that 500,000 credit cards have been stolen.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们已经输掉了这场战役。

sentences.en: I mean, what can we do?
sentences.zh: 我认为几乎发生的情况是，所有这些技术都推出了，所有这些新形式的数据、新形式的互动都推出了。

sentences.en: I don't think we've lost the battle already.
sentences.zh: 像安全这样的问题并没有被真正考虑进去。

sentences.en: I think what's almost happened is that all this technology rolled out, all these new forms of data, new forms of interacting rolled out.
sentences.zh: 像隐私这样的问题也没有被真正考虑进去。

sentences.en: Things like security weren't really considered.
sentences.zh: 显然，这是人们相互交流的新方式，所以人们只是没有对周围的风险有那么高的意识。

sentences.en: Things like privacy weren't really considered.
sentences.zh: 而现在这一切几乎才刚刚开始追赶上来。

sentences.en: Obviously it was a new way of people communicating with each other, so people just weren't aware of the risks around it that much.
sentences.zh: 所以经历了一段推出新事物的时期。

sentences.en: And it's almost like that's now just starting to catch up.
sentences.zh: 噢，是的，让我们试一试吧。

sentences.en: So you've had a period of time where something new has been rolled out.
sentences.zh: 现在我们突然开始看到所有这些新闻报道，因为显然罪犯们意识到

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, let's have a go.
sentences.zh: 他们可以利用某些东西，或者其他人意识到他们可以利用某些东西。

sentences.en: And now we're suddenly starting to see all these stories because obviously the criminals are aware
sentences.zh: 我想我们现在几乎到了这样一个阶段：所有这些风险都在四处蔓延，人们也意识到了它们。

sentences.en: that they can exploit certain things or other people are aware they can exploit certain things.
sentences.zh: 所以剑桥分析公司就是一个很好的例子，它在媒体上被大量报道，引发了报纸上的各种相关故事。

sentences.en: And I think we're almost now at a point where all of these risks are now circulating and people are aware of them.
sentences.zh: 噢，你需要你的Facebook账户吗？

sentences.en: So Cambridge Analytica, that's quite a good example of something that's massively in the media, led to all these stories in newspapers and stuff.
sentences.zh: 也许我们应该停止使用Facebook。

sentences.en: Oh, do you need your Facebook account?
sentences.zh: 你该如何保证它的安全？

sentences.en: Maybe we should stop doing Facebook.
sentences.zh: 事实上，那是数据，你放到社交媒体上的那些数据被其他人使用，并且可以被利用。

sentences.en: How can you secure it?
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上帮助人们理解了这样一个事实：他们在网上发布的东西可能包含敏感信息，并可能被他人利用。

sentences.en: Actually, that was data, and that data that you're putting on social media is used by other people and can be used.
sentences.zh: 所以我其实觉得，我们现在几乎到了这样一个节点：也许这场战役曾经有点失守，但它现在几乎又开始迎头赶上了。

sentences.en: It's been massively helpful to make people understand that actually the stuff they put online is sensitive information potentially and can be used by others.
sentences.zh: 有了新的推动力。

sentences.en: So I actually think we're almost at a point where maybe the battle was being lost a little bit, but it's almost starting to catch up again.
sentences.zh: 显然有很多监管措施，重点都在于改善监管之类的事情。

sentences.en: There's a new impetus.
sentences.zh: 那么我们现在如何才能拥有能够赶上这些新兴数据形式的监管措施呢？

sentences.en: There's obviously a lot of regulation, focus on improving regulation and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们几乎处于——我不想说是转折点，这个词太强烈了——但算是一种转变关头，即：好的，现在风险非常真实，

sentences.en: So how can we now have regulation that catches up with these new forms of data?
sentences.zh: 人们正在看到这一点，我们开始看到更多的全社会层面的回应。

sentences.en: So I think we're almost at, I don't want to say a tipping point, that's very strong, but a kind of turning point where it's like, okay, now the risks are very real
sentences.zh: 所以这将会如何发展我不知道，但我认为我们现在正处于这样一个阶段：是的，也许我们在对抗它们的战役中做得更好了。

sentences.en: and people are seeing that and we're starting to see a more societal response.
sentences.zh: 我希望如此。

sentences.en: So how that will play out, I don't know, but I think we're now at a point where, yeah, maybe we're doing better in the battle.
sentences.zh: 那么你现在在研究什么？

sentences.en: I would hope.
sentences.zh: 你对未来有什么展望？

sentences.en: So what are you studying now?
sentences.zh: 我们正在做一些不同的事情。

sentences.en: What are you looking at for the future?
sentences.zh: 我们正在研究人们如何看待围绕新兴技术的风险，比如自动驾驶汽车，他们是否真的察觉到了与之相关的任何安全风险，

sentences.en: So we're doing a few different things.
sentences.zh: 并且是否在积极应对。

sentences.en: We're looking at how people perceive risks around emerging technologies, so things like autonomous vehicles, whether they actually perceive any security risks associated with that,
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，技术总是在不断发展。

sentences.en: how willing they would be to use those technologies if they became available.
sentences.zh: 他们一旦能够使用这些技术，会有多大意愿去使用。

sentences.en: So we're kind of trying to understand, well, what risks are people worried about?
sentences.zh: 所以我们其实在试着去了解，嗯，大家到底在担心什么风险？

sentences.en: Can we actually almost, before these technologies get rolled out mainstream, let's actually look at how they might be exploited or manipulated,
sentences.zh: 我们能不能在这些技术全面普及之前，实际去看看它们可能会被如何利用或操纵，

sentences.en: how people perceive risks around them and almost kind of then build it into the system so that we can prevent those risks almost becoming a reality.
sentences.zh: 看看人们如何看待周边的风险，然后把这些纳入系统设计中，从而防止这些风险变成现实。

sentences.en: We're also doing some work around how we can better inform people around digital risks, online risks.
sentences.zh: 我们也在做一些工作，探讨如何更好地向人们普及数字风险和网络风险的知识。

sentences.en: So it's quite a technical thing to understand sometimes.
sentences.zh: 所以有时候这确实是一个很技术性的问题。

sentences.en: The online world is really complicated.
sentences.zh: 网络世界真的很复杂。

sentences.en: It's a very complex, abstract beast, really, to try and get your head around.
sentences.zh: 要真正搞懂它，其实是一个非常复杂、抽象的东西。

sentences.en: So we're trying to look at, well, how do people want to be informed about digital risks, online risks?
sentences.zh: 所以我们试图探讨的是，人们究竟希望如何被告知数字风险、网络风险？

sentences.en: How can we empower them to make decisions?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何赋能他们来做决策？

sentences.en: What kind of information do they want to know?
sentences.zh: 他们到底想了解什么样的信息？

sentences.en: How can we best present it to actually encourage them to really make decisions that are going to be in their best interest, I suppose?
sentences.zh: 我们又该如何以最佳方式呈现这些信息，来真正鼓励他们做出符合自身利益的决策呢？

sentences.en: So we're very early stages trying to look at, I suppose, slightly conversation about how people want to be talked about their data
sentences.zh: 所以我们还处于非常初期的阶段，我想，还在探讨人们希望别人如何跟他们谈论数据，

sentences.en: and how we can better design kind of awareness interventions and things to really encourage people to engage with those materials and actually change their behaviour slightly.
sentences.zh: 以及我们该如何更好地设计认知干预措施之类的方法，来真正鼓励人们接触这些材料并稍微改变他们的行为。

sentences.en: So you're not quite there yet?
sentences.zh: 所以你们现在还没做到那一步？

sentences.en: No, gosh, no, no.
sentences.zh: 没有，天哪，完全没有。

sentences.en: No, I think we're very early stage.
sentences.zh: 不，我觉得我们还处在非常初期的阶段。

sentences.en: So I've only just started doing this work at the University of Bristol.
sentences.zh: 所以我才刚开始在布里斯托尔大学开展这项工作。

sentences.en: So I started there last November.
sentences.zh: 我是去年11月开始在那儿工作的。

sentences.en: So before then, I was at the University of Bath doing work around phishing emails and what makes people susceptible to them.
sentences.zh: 在那之前，我在巴斯大学从事钓鱼邮件以及是什么让人容易受其影响的研究。

sentences.en: So that was the stuff focused on influence techniques and whether people notice differences in cues and what factors might affect that in the work environment and stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以那项研究主要关注影响力技术、人们是否能注意到线索的差异，以及工作环境中的哪些因素会对此产生影响等内容。

sentences.en: Whereas now, very much moving into the, since I've started at the University of Bristol, moving into this,
sentences.zh: 而现在，自从我开始在布里斯托尔大学工作以来，很大程度上转向了另一个方向，

sentences.en: OK, how do people perceive risks?
sentences.zh: 也就是：人们是如何看待风险的？

sentences.en: How do they consider them in relation to the online space?
sentences.zh: 他们在网络空间中是如何看待这些风险的？

sentences.en: How do they understand them?
sentences.zh: 他们是如何理解这些风险的？

sentences.en: And if they actually consider it to be quite risky, then what will actually change their behaviour?
sentences.zh: 如果他们真的认为这很有风险，那么什么才能真正改变他们的行为？

sentences.en: Because people are concerned about their privacy, but then they still share information.
sentences.zh: 因为人们一方面关心自己的隐私，但另一方面却依然在分享信息。

sentences.en: They still do things that kind of counter to what they say they care about.
sentences.zh: 他们做的事情依然与他们口口声声在乎的东西背道而驰。

sentences.en: So it's really trying to understand how people are making those judgments.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的是在试图理解人们是如何做出这些判断的。

sentences.en: And that's something we still don't really have a grasp on, I don't think.
sentences.zh: 而这一点，我觉得我们目前仍然没有真正搞懂。

sentences.en: So you said you mentioned Robert Cialdini earlier, and he's done a lot around green behaviour,
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到罗伯特·西奥迪尼，他在绿色行为方面做了很多研究，

sentences.en: people who are aware of the environment and how to make people make decisions that would be earth friendly.
sentences.zh: 研究那些有环保意识的人，以及如何引导人们做出对地球友好的决策。

sentences.en: Is that the kind of information you're looking at?
sentences.zh: 这就是你们正在研究的那类信息吗？

sentences.en: How does that apply to online behaviour?
sentences.zh: 这又是如何应用于网络行为的呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 对，对，我想是的。

sentences.en: Well, in some ways, there's quite a lot of parallels.
sentences.zh: 嗯，从某种程度上讲，有很多相似之处。

sentences.en: So obviously, when we talk about things like environmental behaviours, again, it can be something that's quite far down the line.
sentences.zh: 很显然，当我们谈论环保行为之类的事情时，它同样可能是相对长远的事情。

sentences.en: As a potential, if we take climate change as a potential risk, that's something that people might not necessarily see as happening to me right now in front of me.
sentences.zh: 如果把气候变化当作一种潜在风险，这可能是人们不一定会觉得“此刻正发生在我眼前”的事情。

sentences.en: It's a potential risk in the future.
sentences.zh: 这是未来的潜在风险。

sentences.en: It's something that's quite abstract, it's quite big, who knows who it will apply to or how.
sentences.zh: 它相当抽象，规模很大，谁也不知道它会降临在谁身上，或者会以什么方式降临。

sentences.en: So it can be quite hard when people are actually making a decision in the here and now
sentences.zh: 所以在此时此刻做决定时，人们往往很难去践行某种他们想做、但可能违背环保的行为。

sentences.en: to engage in a behaviour that they want to engage in, but might be counter to obviously environmental, pro-environmental behaviour.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们真的很想这么做。

sentences.en: But they really want to do that.
sentences.zh: 但因为另一件事非常遥远且抽象，他们最终可能不会做出最符合自身利益的决策。

sentences.en: And because the other thing is quite far away and quite abstract, then maybe they won't actually make the decision that's in those best interests.
sentences.zh: 因此，显而易见，西奥迪尼才对如何以某种方式“推一把”人们感兴趣。

sentences.en: Hence why, obviously, Cialdini is interested in kind of almost nudging people into that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们也在研究如何以类似的方式在网络行为中“推”人们一把。

sentences.en: So there is work around how we can nudge people in a similar way in online behaviour.
sentences.zh: 但目前仍处于非常初期的阶段。

sentences.en: But it's still quite early stages.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们面临一个小问题，那就是尽管有很多相似之处——网络风险潜在来看也是一个相当大的问题。

sentences.en: And I think we've got a slight issue in the fact that although there are a lot of similarities, so it's quite a big issue again, online risk potentially.
sentences.zh: 如果你决定点击电子邮件中的链接，或者访问一个可能是诈骗的网站，你是否会立刻看到对自己的影响，这很难说，

sentences.en: If you decide to click on a link in an email or visit a website that might be fraudulent, whether you're going to see an immediate impact on yourself, who knows,
sentences.zh: 特别是在工作环境中，这种影响可能要在很久以后才会显现。

sentences.en: particularly in a work environment, it might be an impact that's way down the line.
sentences.zh: 你根本不明白它会如何起作用。

sentences.en: You don't really understand how it's going to work.
sentences.zh: 同样，这相当抽象。

sentences.en: Again, it's quite abstract.
sentences.zh: 它真的会影响到我吗？

sentences.en: Is it going to really impact me?
sentences.zh: 可能不会。

sentences.en: Potentially not.
sentences.zh: 我不明白它会怎么影响。

sentences.en: I don't understand how it will.
sentences.zh: 所以这里面有所有这些相似的平行关系。

sentences.en: So there's all these similar types of parallels.
sentences.zh: 因此我想说，我们正开始尝试应用完全相同的方法。

sentences.en: So I would say that we are starting to try and apply exactly the same approaches.
sentences.zh: 但在理解这一点的同时，我们也明白技术一直在变，而这正是问题的一部分，因为它发展得太快了。

sentences.en: But whilst also understanding that technology keeps changing, and that's part of the problem, because it's advancing so faSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你观察人们在一个领域的行为，转眼间他们就在使用新技术、使用新的社交媒体平台，甚至比如Facebook变了，

sentences.en: If you look at people's behaviour in one space, suddenly they're using a new technology or they're using a new social media platform or even, for instance, Facebook's changed,
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，甚至一年前的布局跟他们第二年做的事情也会大不相同。

sentences.en: so actually even the layout of one year might be very different to what they're doing next year.
sentences.zh: 这让人很难跟上步伐。

sentences.en: And that makes it very hard to keep up.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为在这方面略有不同，如果这么说能说得通的话。

sentences.en: So it's slightly different in that respect, I would say, if that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 不，说的通。

sentences.en: No, it does.
sentences.zh: 确实说得通。

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 而且你永远不知道。

sentences.en: And you never know.
sentences.zh: 下周就会冒出一个新应用，你突然就迷上了它，而谁知道它在做什么呢。

sentences.en: There's a new app next week that you suddenly are enamoured of, and who knows what it's doing.
sentences.zh: 所以基本的建议是：经常更改密码。

sentences.en: So basic advice, change your passwords often.
sentences.zh: 保持密码足够复杂。

sentences.en: Keep them really complicated.
sentences.zh: 不要把它们写在任何人都能找到的地方。

sentences.en: Don't write them down where anybody can find them.
sentences.zh: 是的，诸如此类的基本常识。

sentences.en: Yeah, basic things like that.
sentences.zh: 不过英国现在有一些建议实际上表明，你其实不应该再那么频繁地更改密码了，因为这让……

sentences.en: Although there is advice now in the UK that actually suggests you shouldn't change your password that often anymore because it's making it very difficult to...
sentences.zh: 你需要复杂密码这一事实是很重要的。

sentences.en: The fact that you need complicated passwords is important.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你还要求人们非常频繁地更改密码，有一种观点认为这两者是矛盾的。

sentences.en: So if you're also requiring people to change them really often, there's a little bit of a school of thought that the two don't marry up.
sentences.zh: 你既不能一直换密码，又要有复杂的密码，还要能记住它们。

sentences.en: You can't keep changing your passwords and have complicated passwords and remember them.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你鼓励人们过于频繁地更改密码，他们可能就会把密码设得更简单，以便更容易记住。

sentences.en: So if you encourage people to change their passwords too often, then they'll maybe just make them simpler so that they can remember them easier.
sentences.zh: 因此，现在有一种更主流的观点认为，你其实不需要那么频繁地更改密码，但你真正需要做的是：

sentences.en: So they actually have more of a school of thought now that you don't need to change them that often, but what you do need to do is have very different passwords
sentences.zh: 针对不同类型的用途，使用非常不同的密码。

sentences.en: for different types of things.
sentences.zh: 所以请确保你的密码截然不同，比如你的网银，或者某种……

sentences.en: So make sure you have very different passwords for, for instance, your banking or something that is very...
sentences.zh: 可能包含关于你大量敏感信息的在线账户，要区别于那种，我不知道，可能是社交媒体之类的账户，

sentences.en: potentially has very sensitive information about yourself to an online account for something, I don't know, maybe social media or something,
sentences.zh: 因为社交媒体并没有把所有这些信息都关联在一起。

sentences.en: where you don't have all that information linked to it.
sentences.zh: 所以这几乎是要去理解风险：嗯，如果有人拿到了那个密码会怎么样？

sentences.en: So it's almost about understanding the risk, well, what if someone had that password?
sentences.zh: 他们能做出的最坏事情是什么？

sentences.en: What is the worst they could do?
sentences.zh: 可能吧，或者如果他们拿到了我的推特密码，他们能做出的最坏事情是什么？

sentences.en: Potentially, or if they have my Twitter password, what's the worst they could do?
sentences.zh: 而且千万不要在不同类型的账户之间使用相同的密码。

sentences.en: And certainly don't use the same passwords across different types of accounts.
sentences.zh: 这是最重要的一点。

sentences.en: That's the big one.
sentences.zh: 对，如果他们黑进了你的推特，你知道的，然后他们还能黑进你的网银，那就真的很不妙了。

sentences.en: Yeah, if they get into your Twitter, you know, and then they can also get into your banking, then it's really not good.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这确实有太多需要操心的事情了。

sentences.en: All right, well, that's a lot to worry about.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Well, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 希望我已经把大家都吓坏了，对吧？

sentences.en: I hope I've got terrified, aren't I?
sentences.zh: 可不是嘛。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 倒也没有那么糟糕。

sentences.en: It's not all bad.
sentences.zh: 我们正在逐步攻克。

sentences.en: We're getting there.
sentences.zh: 那就好。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: I appreciate that.
sentences.zh: 也非常感谢你今天来到我们节目中。

sentences.en: And thank you so much for being with us today.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: No problem.
sentences.zh: 一点问题也没有。

sentences.en: No problem at all.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: Thank you for inviting me.
sentences.zh: 那么谢谢你今天收听我们的播客《心理学话你知》（Speaking of Psychology）。

sentences.en: So thank you for joining us today on our podcast, Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 这是美国心理学协会播客网络的一部分，其中还包括其他精彩的播客，比如探讨最新、最激动人心的心理学研究的《美国心理学协会期刊对话》（APA Journals Dialogue），

sentences.en: This is part of the APA Podcast Network, which includes other great podcasts, such as APA Journals Dialogue about the latest and most exciting psychological research,
sentences.zh: 以及探讨心理学实践的《进展记录》（Progress Notes）。

sentences.en: and Progress Notes, which discusses the practice of psychology.
sentences.zh: 你可以在iTunes、Stitcher上找到所有美国心理学协会的播客，基本上你在哪听播客就在哪能找到。

sentences.en: You can find all APA podcasts on iTunes, Stitcher, and pretty much wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 你也可以访问我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org，收听更多单集并获取我们讨论主题的更多资源。

sentences.en: You can also go to our website, www.speakingofpsychology.org, to listen to more episodes and to see more resources on the topics we discuss.
sentences.zh: 我是来自美国心理学协会的金·米尔斯（Kim Mills），这里是《心理学话你知》。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills with the American Psychological Association, and this is Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: （注：最后一句中的“Speaking of Psychology”保留英文节目名或按常规范本处理，此处直接对应。）
